nodes.name: SBNC03 Solid State Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Nb₂O₅ (99.99%), Ba(NO₃)₂ (≥99%), Sr(NO₃)₂ (≥99%), and Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (≥98%) were mixed homogeneously in stoichiometric ratios according to the formula Sr₀.₅Ba₀.₅Nb₁.₇Co₀.₃O₆ (SBNC03). Subsequently, the mixed powders were pressed into pellets under axial pressure (8 MPa) and then heat-treated at 700°C for 2 h in a muffle furnace. Thereafter, these pellets were reground into fine powders and repressed into pellets under axial pressure (12 MPa), followed by sintering at 1250°C for 12 h in a muffle furnace.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples well crystallized in ferroelectric TTB structure (P4bm) with unit cell enlarged by K filling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) patterns of the as-prepared samples are shown in Figure 3a. Small refinement parameters ... suggest that all the samples are well crystallized in the ferroelectric TTB structure at room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: K0.4SBNC03 shows highly organized single crystallinity with d-spacings of 0.33 nm (201) and 0.62 nm (200) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images of K0.4SBNC03 in Figure 3b,c show the highly organized single crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show polycrystalline particles ≈5 μm in size with broad size distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images in Figure S5 (Supporting Information) provide information on the morphology of the samples. They are polycrystalline particles ≈5 μm in size.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples have relatively small Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area <1 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Technically, all the samples have a relatively small Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area (<1 m² g⁻¹, but impossible to accurately measure).

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show Co²⁺ oxidation state matching CoO standard.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of the Co L₃-edge were collected ... the spectral features of all the samples coincide with that of the standard CoO(Co²⁺).

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s spectra show lattice oxygen (≈530.1-530.9 eV), oxygen vacancies, and surface-adsorbed oxygen; K-containing samples show +0.8 eV blueshift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectra of all the samples can be fitted with three peaks: the first peak is attributed to the electron transition of lattice oxygen ... the spectra of K-containing samples have a blueshift with a value of +0.8 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Band tilting values are 1.09 eV (SBNC03), 2.16 eV (K0.2SBNC03), and 1.73 eV (K0.4SBNC03); remarkable signals from BE=0 eV confirm metallic states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkable signals are detected from BE = 0 eV on all samples, indicating that the difference between VBM and EF approaches zero... the band tilting is 1.09, 2.16, and 1.73 eV for SBNC03, K0.2SBNC03, and K0.4SBNC03 respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Remnant polarization 2Pr increases from 1.3 μC cm⁻² for SBNC03 to 8.76 μC cm⁻² for K0.4SBNC03 with K filling.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 2Pr measured on SBNC03 is 1.3 μC cm⁻² and 8.76 μC cm⁻² for K0.4SBNC03. Although the experimental polarization is slightly smaller than the theoretically calculated one, they have the same trend, in which the ferroelectricity is enhanced with the K filling.

nodes.characterization_summary: K filling has greater impact on c-axis of the lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra in Figure S7 (Supporting Information) indicate that K filling has a greater impact on the c axis of the lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: K, Sr, Ba, Nb, and Co elements distributed homogenously throughout particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping in Figure S6 (Supporting Information) suggests that the K, Sr, Ba, Nb, and Co elements are distributed homogenously.
